Primary Sitrin et al.1985 isolated aridicins A/B/C separately by preparative HPLC and characterized B (Table1 empirical formula C82H84N8O30Cl4). Chung et al.1986 printed652 explicitly states aridicin was renamed ardacin, and Figure1 distinguishes the B factor. This is not an exact or broader relation to generic NCIT:C169786 or CHEBI:753252 ardacin complex; those terms lack an independently inspected factor-B definition. No supplier, pure preparation, CAS or reconstructed stereostructure is invented. ## Limits And Additional Notes

- The frozen duplicate-identifier baseline check fails on exactly the retired CHEBI86477 family; this failure is retained, not waived. The unchanged checker passes against the explicit one-row proposed data-ledger companion in a separate private fixture. Canonical baseline and gates are unchanged.
- All actual read scopes, failed retrievals and native document drafts remain in reviewer artifacts. Abstract-only and methods-only inspections are not described as full-paper reviews.
- Retained historical human mapping evidence and provisional roles remain unchanged and unapproved; newly agent-authored human-only evidence is corrected claim by claim.
- Source-stated unusual hydrates may use distinct local registry identities with honest formal-transcription caveats; no universal crystallography or supplier prerequisite is invented.
- Known source alternatives, unknown product/preparation identity and unresolved quantity discrepancies remain explicit.
- Terminal candidate finding dispositions refer to isolated successor bytes and cannot close GitHub issues, accept whole maintained owners or authorize exports.

    source and current no-glutamine21540 comparator without a primary crosswalk. A
    second source-qualified owner could overlap the historical product; different
    citation names do not establish distinct substances. Only the specifically catalog-bound36
    product is proposed, and no extra owner is minted for0.

    CHEBI:63125 defines the trisodium salt, distinct from disodium CHEBI:64734/64758.

    is chemically wrong. Add the explicit 3Na spelling and retain the wrong disodium
    string only as rejected provenance; no interpretation of case125 is imported here.
    Original NBRC387/900/391 all corroborate3Na-EDTA; NBRC387 specifies200mg in a
    vitamin stock, not the frozen200g/L flattened component.

  area: identity

  outcome: supported
  summary: 'All seven occurrences denote filtered natural seawater as an input before
    mixing or autoclaving. CCAP MErds/NSS low require filling to one litre with it;
    MY75S and ZM10 explicitly dilute that input. NSS low and 2SNA allow synthetic
    salt alternatives, which remain separate alternatives. This scoped input is consistent
    with the Filtered Seawater owner; final-medium dilution and autoclaving do not
    turn its input label into a different source ingredient. Final-review qualification
    of the historical #260 dilution rationale: the original CCAP PE footnote explicitly
    says to filter natural seawater, reduce it to 95% using glass distilled water,
    and autoclave. That prepared input is then dosed at 950 cm3; the prior dilution
    is not inferred from the receiving-medium dose. The literal 95%-strength label
    is retained as REJECTED_LABEL on this bare filtered-seawater owner, without inventing
    the percentage basis, final volume, component ratio or a new preparation owner.
    The unqualified Natural seawater alias is also nonresolving: its recovered JCM1377
    contexts state natural seawater without filtration. Supported Filtered natural
    seawater and Natural seawater (filtrated) aliases remain. Earlier #260 mapping
    evidence and histories are preserved as historical rationale, superseded only
    on these alias applicability points by this source-backed qualification. The two
    assigned filtered cases are not reinterpreted as the 95% preparation. Sources:
    https://www.ccap.ac.uk/wp-content/uploads/MR_PE.pdf ; https://www.jcm.riken.jp/cgi-bin/jcm/jcm_grmd?GRMD=1377
    .'

- assessment_id: CASE-13
  area: identity
  topic: Complete source-case disposition and applicability
  outcome: concern
  summary: The 13 frozen occurrences span freshwater electron-acceptor media and BG11
    derivatives. Lovley1988 p1473 specifies Fe(III)-citrate 20 mM. The newly inspected
    Coppi2001 FWAFC methods specify 55.9 mM Fe(III) citrate and print 13.7 g FeC6O7/L;
    Risso2009 culture methods specify ferric citrate 56 mM. These recovered ferric-citrate
    inputs do not establish the shared two-ligand CHEBI:4991 ion or validate KEGG:fe3dcit
    as a KEGG compound accession. Labarre1987 pp4668–4669 and Anderson1991 pp2761–2762
    name BG11 and modifications without specifying the citrate reagent in those inspected
    methods. Park2005 supplied an explicit subscription preview rather than methods;
    its Europe PMC request timed out. Shcolnick2007 metadata/abstract was read, while
    the ScienceDirect full-article route returned HTTP403/CPE00001. The referenced
    Rippka1979 full-text route returned HTTP403 with a JavaScript/cookie challenge.
    These are route-specific limits, not a blanket claim that primary methods are
    unavailable. The exact shared dicitrate association remains held pending per-occurrence
    source-to-model identity reconciliation; neither one freshwater formulation nor
    an unverified BG11 recipe may be applied to all 13 occurrences.

    more specific peeled/cut material proposal. Starting potato masses are process

    and filter through cheesecloth. Those outputs remain distinct; the record describes
    the peeled/cut tissue before extraction.

    values remain distinct evidence.

  outcome: concern
  summary: D-glutamate is stereospecific and cannot map to L or unspecified glutamate.
    CHEBI:29986 is D-glutamate(1-) with both carboxylates anionic and amino group
    protonated. The MediaDB source links include KEGG:glu-D model shorthand, and three
    recipes do not establish whether the source meant an acid, salt, or modeled ion;
    no original reagent form is documented. Directly inspected Lee2009 full text Table4
    row13 specifies L-glutamic acid250mg, and its methods say AAM-minus omits L-glutamic
    acid. This directly contradicts frozen MediaDB292 AAM-minus D-glutamate1.71mM.
    Klein1979 publisher landing page is public, but its linked full-text endpoint
    returned403; original D stereochemistry remains unverified for its two occurrences.

  summary: 'JCM1102 explicitly lists 750 ml Natural seawater (filtrated) as an input
    alongside 250 ml distilled water; all four frozen TOGO variants preserve that
    same input while varying supplements. Filtrated and filtered name the same treatment
    here. The identity candidate is the existing Filtered Seawater material, not the
    complete anaerobic medium or its 75% dilution. Final-review qualification of the
    historical #260 dilution rationale: the original CCAP PE footnote explicitly says
    to filter natural seawater, reduce it to 95% using glass distilled water, and
    autoclave. That prepared input is then dosed at 950 cm3; the prior dilution is
    not inferred from the receiving-medium dose. The literal 95%-strength label is
    retained as REJECTED_LABEL on this bare filtered-seawater owner, without inventing
    the percentage basis, final volume, component ratio or a new preparation owner.
    The unqualified Natural seawater alias is also nonresolving: its recovered JCM1377
    contexts state natural seawater without filtration. Supported Filtered natural
    seawater and Natural seawater (filtrated) aliases remain. Earlier #260 mapping
    evidence and histories are preserved as historical rationale, superseded only
    on these alias applicability points by this source-backed qualification. The two
    assigned filtered cases are not reinterpreted as the 95% preparation. Sources:
    https://www.ccap.ac.uk/wp-content/uploads/MR_PE.pdf ; https://www.jcm.riken.jp/cgi-bin/jcm/jcm_grmd?GRMD=1377
    .'

    as5-formyltetrahydrofolic acid,C20H23N7O7; folic27470 isC19H19N7O6. JCM537 also
